summary.text: A 38-year-old man with a 27 pack-year smoking history and 10 years of multidrug abuse, including cocaine twice a week and four joints of cannabis a day, was admitted with palpitations and dizziness. ECG showed a regular wide QRS tachycardia at 220 beats/min with negative concordance, diagnosed as ventricular tachycardia, and urgent electrical cardioversion was performed for hemodynamic instability.

After cardioversion the ECG showed sinus rhythm with complete right bundle branch block and a QRS duration of 160 msec. Hypersensitive troponins were elevated at 2018 ng/L, while CPK, metabolic analyses, inflammatory markers and coronary angiography were normal and viral serology was not performed. TTE showed LVEF 60% with normal global longitudinal strain; CMR showed LVEF 45% with septal hypokinesia and enhancement of the subepicardial lateral wall, suggestive of myocarditis, and toxic myocarditis revealed by VT was diagnosed.

He was referred to a detoxification center and prescribed amiodarone and an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, with CMR reevaluation planned 6 months after onset; beta blockers were not prescribed. At 2 months of follow-up he was asymptomatic and had stopped abusing drugs.

summary.text: A 39-year-old man with a history of heavy smoking (50 pack-years), daily cannabis use for 3 years and monthly cocaine use for under a year presented to the emergency department with new-onset palpitations. ECG showed a regular wide QRS tachycardia with a left bundle branch block pattern, highly suggestive of ventricular tachycardia.

Given stable hemodynamic status, pharmacological cardioversion with a loading dose of intravenous amiodarone was attempted and sinus rhythm was restored. Myocardial enzymes, inflammation markers, ionic analyses and coronary angiography were normal and viral serology was not performed. TTE showed LVEF 60%; CMR within 48 h of presentation showed LVEF 48% with lateral hypokinesia, T2 hypersignal and linear subepicardial enhancement of the lateral wall, and acute toxic myocarditis was the most likely diagnosis.

He was referred to a detoxification center and prescribed amiodarone to prevent arrhythmia recurrence and an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor to avoid further ventricular remodeling, with CMR planned 6 months later; beta blockers were not prescribed. On reexamination he had withheld drug abuse, begun a smoking cessation plan, remained asymptomatic and his ECG was unchanged.
